findings.title: TotalDocs iterates the cache map without any lock while BuildIndex now writes concurrently
findings.body: The PR removes the cacheMu lock that previously wrapped the entire BuildIndex, so b.cache is now written (line 138, under Lock) while TotalDocs (lines 144-154) iterates b.cache with no lock at all. searchSupport.init() calls TotalDocs right after a concurrent errgroup build, and init() is now invoked synchronously at server startup where builds run with s.initWorkers goroutines, so a concurrent map read/write here is a realistic scenario and will crash the process with 'fatal error: concurrent map read and map write'.

findings.title: Dropping the build-wide lock allows duplicate concurrent builds of the same index
findings.body: Previously cacheMu was held for the whole BuildIndex, guaranteeing only one build per key. Now the lock is only taken for the final map assignment, so two callers (e.g. getOrCreateIndex racing with init, or two searches for an unbuilt namespace) can both build the same NamespacedResource simultaneously. For file-based indexes both call bleve.New on the same directory path, which will fail or corrupt the on-disk index; for memory indexes one built index is silently overwritten in the cache (leaking the other and double-counting IndexTenants/IndexedKinds metrics). A per-key build lock or singleflight is needed now that the coarse lock is gone.

findings.title: errgroup goroutines race on shared err and totalBatchesIndexed variables
findings.body: Inside searchSupport.init(), each group.Go closure executes `_, _, err = s.build(...)` assigning to the outer `err` variable shared by all goroutines, and does `totalBatchesIndexed++` on a shared int. Both are unsynchronized concurrent accesses (a data race detectable by -race) and the write to the outer err can clobber the real error before group.Wait() returns, so a failed build could be masked. The closure should use a local error (`_, _, berr := s.build(...); return berr`) and an atomic counter.

findings.title: Test can panic calling err.Error() on a nil error from ms.Run()
findings.body: The goroutine does `err = ms.Run(); if err.Error() != "context canceled"`. If Run() ever returns nil, err.Error() panics in the goroutine and crashes the test binary rather than failing the test cleanly. It should check `if err != nil && err.Error() != ...` or use require.Error. (Not introduced by this PR, but the test is being modified here.)
